newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends little changed, gilt prices harden.
newsitem.headline: India call ends little changed, gilt prices harden.

text.p: Indian call money ended at 0.50 percent on Thursday, marginally higer than the day's opening 0.25-0.50 percent on some late demand for funds, dealers said.
"There was slight deamnd for funds towards close, but nothing major," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There is just too much supply of funds and not enough demand."
Dealers said secondary market prices of government securities firmed up in brisk trade. They said demand was concentrated in securities with maturities up to the year 2000.

"With call money rates at current levels, banks are looking to play the securities market," said a dealer. He said volumes traded on the National Stock Exchange rose to 5.16 billion rupees from Wednesday's 4.38 billion.
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded at 103.20 rupees against its last traded price of 103.05 while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock improved to 103.20 from 193.09, dealers said.
Yields on treasury bills also fell as buying interest from banks pushed prices up, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in August yielded nine percent against Wednesday's 9.20 percent while September bill yielded 9.18 percent from 9.45, they said.
